match.reason: None of the bank points teaches foil characters; they cover characterisation methods, dynamic and static characters, and dialogue, and do not mention contrasting characters that highlight a main character's traits.

draft.title: Foil characters
card: A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with those of another character, usually the main one. The two are set side by side so the differences are easy to see.
The contrast makes the main character's traits stand out. A reckless friend beside a cautious hero makes the hero's caution seem stronger.
A foil does not have to be an enemy. A foil can be a friend, a sibling or a rival. What matters is the contrast in qualities, such as brave and timid, or honest and deceitful.
To spot a foil, ask which two characters are opposites in some way, and what that contrast shows about each of them.
draft.remember: A foil is a contrasting character who makes another character's traits clearer.

a.q: In an invented novel, Ravi is quiet and thinks before he speaks. His cousin Dev is loud and speaks without thinking. What is Dev's main role beside Ravi?
opts: A foil, whose contrast makes Ravi's traits stand out
A villain, who stops Ravi from reaching his goal
A narrator, who tells the reader what Ravi thinks
A symbol, who stands for the setting of the story
a.why: Dev's loud, impulsive nature contrasts with Ravi's quiet, thoughtful nature, so Ravi's calm is easier to notice. Dev is not a villain: a foil only needs to contrast, and nothing says he opposes Ravi's goals.
a.clue: Look at how the two cousins differ in qualities.

b.q: In a short story, Mia admits her mistakes and takes the blame. Her best friend Jess lies to avoid trouble, and the two are close. Which statement about Jess is the most accurate?
opts: A foil, because her lying contrasts with Mia's honesty
Not a foil, because she and Mia are close friends
A foil, because she and Mia share the same qualities
Not a foil, because a foil must be the main character
b.why: Jess's lying contrasts with Mia's honesty, which makes Mia's honesty clearer. Friendship does not stop Jess being a foil, because a foil is about contrasting qualities, not opposition.
b.clue: Does a foil need to be an enemy?

a.best: A foil, whose contrast makes Ravi's traits stand out

b.best: A foil, because her lying contrasts with Mia's honesty
